name: Vein Dedicated Server
description: Install the official Vein dedicated server through SteamCMD and launch its native Windows server executable directly without a shell.
known_limitations: Console commands and a documented graceful shutdown procedure are marked "to be determined" in the upstream wiki. This template uses terminate as a bounded fallback and does not claim graceful-save semantics.
No dedicated configuration file is documented upstream. Server name, admin/whitelist management, and save handling are not exposed as GameNode variables.
The upstream server requires the Visual C++ 2012/2013/2015-2022 redistributables and DirectX End-User Runtimes on the host; GameNode does not install these prerequisites.
Upstream references an optional TCP RCON listener on the game port without documenting how to enable or authenticate it; this template does not configure or use RCON.
SteamCMD supports initial installation and explicit manual updates through GameNode's Update Server action; automatic, scheduled, and update-on-start updates are not enabled.
Only the documented 64-bit Windows build is advertised; Linux is not offered upstream.

variables.name: Server port
variables.description: Primary UDP game port players connect to.

variables.name: Query port
variables.description: UDP port used for the Steam server browser query. Cannot be set between 27020 and 27050; Steam reserves that range for local use.

variables.name: Maximum players
variables.description: Player cap passed on the command line. Upstream's own default is 64.

ports.name: Game RCON TCP
ports.purpose: Optional remote console access documented on the same port number as the game port; GameNode does not configure or use it

requirements.description: The dedicated server is documented for 64-bit Windows only; no Linux build is currently offered upstream.
Managed SteamCMD with anonymous login is required for installation.
VeinServer-Win64-Test.exe is a 64-bit executable and will not run on a 32-bit host.
Reserve at least 5 GB for server files plus additional space for saves and future updates, per upstream documentation.
The host must have the Visual C++ 2012/2013/2015-2022 redistributables and DirectX End-User Runtimes installed; GameNode does not install these.
Upstream documents at least 8 GB of RAM for an empty server; usage grows with connected players, mods, and settings.

help.summary: GameNode installs Steam App 2131400 anonymously and launches VeinServer-Win64-Test.exe directly without a batch file or shell. Game port, query port, and max players are edited in the server's Configuration tab.
notes: Upstream documents at least 8 GB of RAM as the minimum for an empty server; usage grows with connected players, mods, and settings.
The query port cannot fall between 27020 and 27050 because Steam reserves that range for local use.
Console commands and a documented graceful shutdown path are marked "to be determined" in the official wiki, so this template uses terminate as a bounded fallback.
Only a 64-bit Windows build is published upstream; Linux is not advertised by this template.

findings.summary: Upstream does not document a console command, RCON command, or signal for graceful shutdown, so GameNode's native terminate lifecycle is used without a save guarantee.
No dedicated server configuration file is documented upstream; all managed settings are passed as process arguments.
Upstream references an optional TCP RCON listener on the game port without documenting how to enable or authenticate it; this template does not configure RCON.

prerequisites: Network access to Steam content servers
64-bit Windows host with the Visual C++ 2012/2013/2015-2022 redistributables and DirectX End-User Runtimes installed
At least 8 GB RAM and 5 GB of free disk space
